business.description: Kokuyo Camlin Limited is engaged in the business of manufacturing and selling stationery and art materials. The company has over 55 years of experience in marketing, administration, and overall management.

products.name: Writing Instruments
products.note: Pens and pencils account for the largest share by volume, with demand remaining stable. Differentiation driven by branding, ink quality, and ergonomic design.

products.name: Notebooks and Paper Products
products.note: Notebooks contribute significantly to industry value, with demand peaking during academic cycles. Sustainability considerations influencing paper sourcing and recycling practices.

products.name: Office Stationery
products.note: Includes files, folders, paper, and desk accessories. Demand largely driven by government institutions and MSMEs, ensuring consistency.

products.name: Art and Creative Supplies
products.note: Smaller but faster-growing segment, driven by rising interest in hobbies, school art education, and creative professionals. Offers higher potential for premiumisation and value-added products.

products.name: Consumer products (stationery items including fine arts & hobby products, scholastic products, markers, notebooks, technical instruments, adhesives, etc.)
Art and creative materials, stationery products
products.note: Products carry CE marking (European safety/environmental standards), ISI mark (BIS compliance), and plastic recycle marks on packaging

products.note: Purchase of stock-in-trade for stationery items was Rs 16,930.95 lakhs in FY2026 and Rs 16,447.04 lakhs in FY2025

outlook.statement: Future plan of action envisages acceleration in the process of development already set in motion and undertaking further process development work for achieving cost reduction, creating innovative products and improvement in quality.
Looking ahead, the company started to enhance its engineering and moulding technologies.

In the short term (2026–2027), India's stationery industry is expected to maintain stable demand, driven by the education sector and examination cycles. Growth is likely to be supported by gradual premiumisation, with organised players continuing to strengthen their presence, particularly in urban markets.

Over the medium term, the industry could reach approximately ₹60,000 crore by 2030, led by sustained education demand, expansion of premium and creative segments, and stronger brand differentiation. While volume growth may remain moderate, steady value growth is expected.

No risks which in the opinion of the Board threaten the existence of the Company. However, some risks which may pose challenges are set out in the Management Discussion and Analysis Report.
Shift in Consumer Preferences: Evolving consumer behaviour driven by digital adoption and lifestyle changes may impact demand for traditional stationery and art products.
Raw Material Cost Fluctuation: Variability in global supply chains and inflationary pressures, including geopolitical disruptions, may result in increased input costs, affecting margins.
Demand Seasonality: Sales performance is influenced by academic cycles and festive periods, resulting in seasonal fluctuations in demand.
Brand Relevance: Sustaining brand resonance among younger and digitally engaged consumers remains essential in a competitive environment.
Regulatory and Policy Changes: Changes in education policies, trade regulations, and environmental norms may impact compliance requirements and operational processes.
Competitive Environment: Intense competition from domestic stationery brands may impact market share, pricing power, and margins.

The Company operates in a dynamic business scenario that gives rise to external and internal risk factors. Some of the risks which may pose challenges are set out in the Management Discussion and Analysis Report.
